## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
In contrast, rival schools maintained that adepts comprehend the truths and eradicate defilements stage by stage [Dutt 1945; Dutt 1978]. According to the *Kathāvatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, the doctrine of gradual realization was championed by the Andhakas, Sabbatthikas (Sarvāstivādins), Sammitiyas, and Bhadrayānikas [Hazra 2002; Ruegg, Buddha-nature].
SuttaCentral records one modern translation and lists cross-references to related themes across canonical and para-canonical works, including the *Odhisokathā* (Kv 1.4), *Aññāṇakathā* (Kv 2.2), *Jīvitāvoropanakathā* (Kv 12.8), *Pahārādasutta* (AN 8.19), *Gavampatisutta* (SN 56.30), *Ratana Sutta* (Snp 2.1), and parallel verses in northern Dharmapadas and Udānavargas [SuttaCentral]. Computational analysis via DharmaNexus reveals widespread Pali-internal text reuse (2,107 matches across 123 texts), largely comprising formulaic argumentation shared with other *Kathāvatthu* chapters—most notably *Odhisokathā* (Kv 1.4, sharing over 37,000 characters, especially §9.5_3–10.3_7), *Vimuccamānakathā* (Kv 3.4), *Aparāpisamannāgatakathā* (Kv 4.9), and *Parihānikathā* (Kv 1.2)—as well as discourses in the Sotāpatti Saṁyutta (SN 55) and Aṅguttara Nikāya (AN 6, AN 8, AN 9) [DharmaNexus]. Outside Pali, DharmaNexus automatically aligns segments of the debate with Tibetan translations of northern scholastic texts, notably Vasubandhu's *Abhidharmakośabhāṣya* (D4090), the *Abhidharmakośaṭīkā* (D4092-2), and the *Āryasaṃdhinirmocanasūtravyākhyāna* (D4358-2) [DharmaNexus].
